about: The questions get-context must answer before any plan. Each answer is the user's, deduced by Claude (and shown to the user), or 'not needed'. Pace is never a question: Claude derives it from tempo, type and risk and writes it in plain words. Claude never edits this file.

questions.ask: What do you want to achieve, and how will we know it is done?
questions.why: defines the last stage and how it is verified

questions.ask: Is it personal, for your company, or for a client?
questions.why: pace, who approves, what goes into git

questions.ask: Who decides the timing? Are there deadlines (final and intermediate)?
What already exists: code, decisions, inherited constraints?
questions.why: Discovery, what is not up for discussion

questions.ask: How costly is a mistake (a demo, a product that must last, sensitive data)?
questions.why: how much to discuss, whether a vault is needed

questions.ask: Budget, mandatory technologies, rules (personal data, NDA)?
What do you decide, and what do you leave to Claude?
Which parts is the work made of (frontend, backend, app, documents...)?
questions.why: parallel work: independent parts get their contracts discussed first

questions.ask: Do we need a decision vault, or is the context card enough?
